_readme: Every line the office slice shows. The key is the line's id: a voice recording saved as res://audio/vo/<id>.ogg plays automatically with that line. Speakers: narrator, adrian, tom.

intro_1.speaker: narrator
intro_1.text: Boston. February, nineteen thirty-nine. The radiator knocked like a debtor and gave nothing back.

intro_2.speaker: narrator
intro_2.text: Four floors up, behind frosted glass that spelled his name backward to him every morning, Adrian Vale kept an office with very little in it.

intro_3.speaker: narrator
intro_3.text: He had time, he judged, for three small things before the day came looking for him.

photo_1.speaker: narrator
photo_1.text: A photograph of a girl of seventeen, caught mid-laugh, as though the camera had told her a bad joke. Sylvia.

photo_2.speaker: narrator
photo_2.text: He talked about his sister to anyone who would sit still long enough. The frame was the only thing in the office he had paid full price for.

envelope_1.speaker: narrator
envelope_1.text: An envelope addressed to Worcester in his own careful hand. Inside, the month's money for home.

envelope_2.speaker: narrator
envelope_2.text: It was always sent. It was never quite enough to stop sending.

pistol_1.speaker: narrator
pistol_1.text: In the bottom drawer, beneath files from cases that had paid in promises, lay a pistol he owned and did not love.

pistol_2.speaker: narrator
pistol_2.text: He had bought it because a man in his line was supposed to. He had never once carried it. Dead witnesses can't talk.

pistol_take.speaker: narrator
pistol_take.text: He weighed it in his palm, then slid it into his coat. It sat there like a held breath.

pistol_leave.speaker: narrator
pistol_leave.text: He closed the drawer. It was not the first time.

gin_1.speaker: narrator
gin_1.text: Behind the third drawer of the filing cabinet: good gin, the bottle two-thirds full.

gin_2.speaker: narrator
gin_2.text: For after work. Never during. It was not yet after.

knife_1.speaker: narrator
knife_1.text: A plain folding knife, long and slim, black-handled. No monogram. No ornament.

knife_2.speaker: narrator
knife_2.text: Just a knife, for opening boxes. He put it in his pocket, as he did every morning.

bills_1.speaker: narrator
bills_1.text: Bills, sorted with great care into the order he intended to ignore them. The rent. The telephone. A tailor who had begun writing in a less friendly hand.

bills_2.speaker: narrator
bills_2.text: The office was afloat, in the way a man treading water is afloat.

already.speaker: narrator
already.text: He had already looked. Looking again would not change it.

no_time.speaker: narrator
no_time.text: There was no more time for small things.

knock_2.speaker: narrator
knock_2.text: Not a client's knock. Clients knocked as though they were apologising. This was a man who had knocked on doors that did not want to open.

tom_enter.speaker: narrator
tom_enter.text: The man in the doorway was broad enough to fill it. His nose had been broken once and set by someone in a hurry, and a scar ran the line of his jaw. He took in the room in one look and did not seem to think much of it.

tom_pistol.speaker: narrator
tom_pistol.text: His eyes went once to the weight in Vale's coat, rested there a moment, and moved on.

tom_1.speaker: tom
tom_1.text: Vale? Garrity. I work for Mr. Edmund Wycliffe.

narr_drink.speaker: narrator
narr_drink.text: Neither, Vale noted, was he. It was the first thing they agreed on.

tom_2.speaker: tom
tom_2.text: Something was taken from his house in Brookline. A hair ornament. White diamonds, made to look like a rose with frost on it. They call it the Winter Rose.

tom_3.speaker: tom
tom_3.text: He'd like it back. Quietly. No police, no newspapers.

narr_why.speaker: narrator
narr_why.text: Garrity said it the way a man reads a line he has been given. He looked at Vale as though Vale were a job he had not yet decided how to do.

tom_4.speaker: tom
tom_4.text: The girl who wears it. The prima at the Civic Ballet, come the spring. And there's a Miss Ashcroft at his museum who knows its history better than he does.

say_haggle.speaker: adrian
say_haggle.text: For a diamond you can't report stolen? Thirty.

bills_fee.speaker: narrator
bills_fee.text: He thought of the tailor's letter, and found his voice.

tom_fee_lose.speaker: tom
tom_fee_lose.text: Twenty. He said you'd haggle, too.

narr_fee_lose.speaker: narrator
narr_fee_lose.text: Garrity's face did not move. It did not need to.

narr_close.speaker: narrator
narr_close.text: The door closed. The office seemed, for a moment, smaller than before.

end_1.speaker: narrator
end_1.text: A stolen rose. A dancer. A museum full of other men's treasures. It was, for the first time in a long while, a case.
